hypothesis: In a contact-center authentication flow, adding voice-based speaker verification plus an active liveness challenge as a step-up factor (treatment) will reduce successful fraudulent account access by at least 30% relative to knowledge-based authentication (baseline), while increasing average handle time and customer drop-off by no more than 10%, when evaluated on comparable call workloads.

baseline.description: Existing risk-based call authentication without biometric voice factors. Callers are authenticated using standard knowledge-based authentication (KBA) and existing account/device risk scores. No speaker verification or voice liveness checks are used.
authentication_flow: Inbound call arrives via telephony/CCaaS platform.
IVR or agent collects account identifier (e.g., phone number, account number).
Risk engine evaluates device, phone number reputation, recent activity, and transaction context.
If risk score < baseline_threshold_low_risk: lightweight KBA (e.g., 1–2 questions) or trust-on-device may be sufficient.
If baseline_threshold_low_risk <= risk score < baseline_threshold_high_risk: standard KBA (e.g., 3–5 questions covering DOB, postal code, recent transactions).
If risk score >= baseline_threshold_high_risk: escalate to enhanced KBA (e.g., one-time password via SMS/email, or callback to registered number).
On successful KBA/OTP, agent or system permits sensitive actions; on failure, call is limited to low-risk actions or terminated.

biometric_and_liveness.voice_biometric_enrollment: Not performed; no stored speaker embeddings or voiceprints.

baseline.journey_placement: Authentication occurs early in the call before allowing profile changes, high-value transfers, or disclosure of sensitive information. Voice is used only for ASR or call recording, not for verification.

inputs: Device/telecom risk (e.g., SIM swap signals, call forwarding flags where available)
Account history (time since last login/call, recent transactions, failed logins)
Geo/IP (for digital channels, if any cross-reference is available)
Channel context (IVR self-service vs. live agent, language, queue type)
risk_engine_integration.decision: Outputs a scalar risk_score_baseline in [0, 1] used to decide level of KBA required.

treatment.description: Layered authentication that introduces voice-based speaker verification and active liveness checks as a step-up factor on top of existing KBA and risk scoring. Voice biometrics are only used where appropriate consent has been captured and stored.
authentication_flow: Inbound call arrives via telephony/CCaaS platform.
IVR or agent collects account identifier; risk engine computes initial risk_score_treatment using the same features and thresholds as baseline.
System checks voice biometric consent and enrollment status for the asserted account.
Branch A (enrolled + consented, low/medium risk):
- System prompts caller to speak a short random phrase or passphrase (text-dependent) or conducts a brief free-speech capture (text-independent), depending on prototype configuration.
- Speaker verification model generates an embedding, compares it against stored template(s), and outputs a similarity score.

- In-medium or high-risk cases, an active liveness challenge is triggered (e.g., challenge phrase with randomized digits/words or simple actions like 'say the color of the word you see in your app now'), collected and scored by a liveness model or rule-based check.
- Risk engine fuses risk_score_treatment, speaker_score, and liveness_score into a combined_auth_risk_score.
- If combined_auth_risk_score < treatment_pass_threshold: reduce KBA burden (e.g., 0–2 questions) and allow sensitive actions; otherwise fall back to enhanced KBA/OTP or partial denial.
Branch B (not enrolled, no consent, or regulatory exclusion):
- Fallback to baseline KBA flow, but with optional soft enrollment invitation if jurisdiction and policy allow.
Branch C (very high risk irrespective of voice):
- Require both successful voice verification+liveness AND an out-of-band factor (OTP or callback) or route to a specialist fraud agent with restricted permissions.

speaker_verification.mode: Prototype supports both text-dependent and text-independent configurations; experimenters must choose one as primary for a given run and keep it constant during measurement.
models: Pre-trained speaker embedding model (e.g., ECAPA-TDNN or x-vector variant) from a public repository such as SpeechBrain or PyTorch Hub.
Simple backend scorer (e.g., cosine similarity over embeddings or PLDA) with thresholds tuned using a held-out dataset.
enrollment_process: Explicit consent capture with jurisdiction-specific language (out of scope for this experiment’s implementation, but must be affirmed in metadata).
Collection of N_enroll utterances per customer (e.g., 3–5 short phrases or 20–30 seconds of speech over one or more calls).
Computation and storage of one or more averaged enrollment embeddings per account.
Storage in a secure, access-controlled feature store with encryption at rest and in transit, plus a revocation flag.

liveness_challenge.type: Active liveness via randomized challenge phrases with unpredictable content that is difficult for real-time voice-cloning systems to synthesize and play back without noticeable latency or artifacts.
challenge_generation: Random selection from challenge templates (e.g., 'Please say: <digit> <color> <weekday>', 'Please repeat: <short phrase> but change the last word to <other word>').
Ensure that phrase content is not published in a static list that an attacker can pre-synthesize; randomness must be derived from a secure PRNG.
Record audio during the challenge window (e.g., 3–6 seconds), tag with challenge_id and expected_text.
verification_methods: ASR-based check that recognized text matches the expected phrase pattern with configurable tolerance.
Timing-based checks (latency between prompt end and speech onset, overall duration).
Optional basic spectral/embedding anomaly heuristics (e.g., compare to natural voice baseline for that caller).

inputs: liveness_score (normalized to [0, 1], including a hard-fail flag if ASR mismatch or impossible timing).
risk_engine_integration.fusion_logic: A configurable function (e.g., logistic regression or weighted linear combination) that outputs combined_auth_risk_score in [0, 1]. The function must be fixed for the duration of the experiment and documented in configuration.
risk_engine_integration.example_fusion: combined_auth_risk_score = w_risk * risk_score_treatment + w_spk * (1 - speaker_verification_score) + w_live * (1 - liveness_score)

treatment.journey_placement: Voice verification and liveness are used as step-up factors only when (a) the caller’s risk score is above a configurable threshold but below a hard-block threshold, and (b) the caller is about to perform medium- or high-risk actions (e.g., funds transfer, adding a new payee, changing email/phone, disclosing sensitive data). Low-risk informational calls are not subjected to biometric checks.

requirements_for_inclusion: Only callers with recorded, auditable biometric consent may be included in treatment speaker verification flows, in jurisdictions where this is legally permitted.

Voice embeddings are stored as regulated data with appropriate access controls; raw audio may be stored or discarded based on local policy but must not be repurposed beyond authentication and fraud defense.

Customers must be able to revoke consent, which disables use of speaker verification for that account and triggers deletion or archiving in accordance with policy; revoked accounts must be treated as baseline for experimentation.

workloads.name: WL1_production_like_live_calls
workloads.description: A live, randomized subset of inbound production calls from consenting, enrolled customers routed either to baseline or treatment flows via an A/B router for a fixed evaluation window.

inclusion_criteria: Customer is already enrolled in voice biometrics with valid consent and at least N_enroll high-quality enrollment utterances.
Call is categorized as medium or high risk based on transaction type or requested operation (e.g., password reset, address change, large transfer).
Jurisdiction and policy permit biometric authentication for this use case.
exclusion_criteria: Known fraud accounts flagged for law-enforcement monitoring (to avoid experiment bias or interference).
Regulatory or contractual prohibitions on biometric processing (e.g., local laws or customer segment opt-outs).
Calls with technical issues affecting audio quality beyond defined thresholds (e.g., excessive packet loss, SNR below configured level).

traffic_allocation.randomization_unit: Call-level randomization stratified by account_id and risk band to balance demographics, languages, and risk distributions across arms.
stratification_variables: risk_band (low/medium/high as defined by baseline risk engine)
device/channel type where available (mobile, landline, VoIP)

workloads.duration: Minimum of 4–6 weeks or until pre-specified sample size for key metrics (e.g., fraud_events) is reached, whichever is longer.
workloads.environment: Production-like telephony and CCaaS environment with the prototype deployed behind feature flags, monitored by observability tooling.
ethical_and_operational_notes: Treatment must not materially reduce security for any subgroup compared with baseline; fail-closed behavior (fallback to baseline or stronger controls) is required on technical errors.
Customers may be informed of voice verification use via standard disclosures; the experiment itself should not rely on deception.

workloads.name: WL2_offline_replay_benchmark
workloads.description: Controlled offline replay of labeled audio sessions (genuine vs. known synthetic/attacker calls) through the baseline and treatment logic to estimate detection performance and thresholds before live deployment.
data_sources: Historical genuine customer calls from consenting, enrolled users with no confirmed fraud during the call window.
Synthetic attacker calls generated via public or in-house voice cloning tools, using the same languages and call scripts, tagged with ground-truth labels.
High-risk fraud calls previously confirmed by investigations, where permissible to use for benchmarking.
usage: Estimate ROC, EER, FAR, and FRR for the speaker verification prototype and liveness challenges.
Tune thresholds for speaker_verification_score and liveness_score before going live.
Perform adversarial spot checks (e.g., attacker playback of cloned voice) independent of production traffic.
workloads.randomization: Offline data will be sampled and split into training, validation, and test partitions; the test partition must not be used for threshold tuning.

randomization_and_assignment: Implement a deterministic randomization function that maps (account_id, call_id, experiment_id) to a uniform random number in [0, 1]; use this to assign each eligible call to baseline or treatment based on allocation_ratios.

Ensure that multiple calls from the same account across the experiment window are consistently assigned to the same arm, unless a deliberate crossover design is used and documented; for the default design, prefer account-level consistency to reduce contamination.
Log assignment decisions with timestamps and configuration version identifiers.
comparability_controls: Monitor and enforce similarity of risk_score distributions across arms using periodic statistical checks; adjust stratification if imbalances emerge.
Ensure that the same risk engine version, thresholds, and non-voice features are used in both arms.
Maintain equivalent agent guidance and scripts except for authentication steps influenced by voice verification; avoid bias from differential coaching.
technical_controls: Run both baseline and treatment pipelines in the same cloud region and infrastructure class to control for latency and availability differences.
Use the same ASR stack for liveness across treatment variants; do not change ASR models mid-experiment without versioning and documentation.
Implement health checks for speaker verification and liveness services; on failure, automatically fall back to baseline KBA for that call and mark it as 'baseline_effective' in logs.
privacy_and_consent_controls: Exclude any call without recorded biometric consent from speaker verification flows; these calls must be routed to baseline logic even if the randomization function selects treatment.
Mask or tokenize personal identifiers in experimental logs; store linkage in a separate, access-controlled system if necessary for later analysis.
Respect data minimization and retention policies; ensure that experimental features do not log more sensitive data than necessary.
governance_controls: Obtain approvals from security, privacy, and legal stakeholders before starting the experiment, including a documented DPIA/PIA where required.
Define an incident response protocol if unexpected increases in fraud or customer complaints are observed in either arm.
Configure real-time monitoring dashboards to detect metric anomalies (e.g., spike in failure-to-authenticate, drop-off) and provide a kill switch to revert all traffic to baseline if needed.

metrics.name: fraud_events
metrics.description: Count of confirmed fraudulent account takeovers or high-impact fraudulent actions initiated via the phone channel during the experiment window, attributed to calls in each arm.
metrics.collection_method: Derived from downstream fraud investigations, chargeback data, and case management labels linked back to original call IDs; requires lag-aware attribution windows.
metrics.aggregation: Per arm, per risk_band, per week.

metrics.name: fraud_rate_per_10k_calls
metrics.description: Number of confirmed fraud_events per 10,000 authenticated calls in a given arm.
metrics.aggregation: Per arm, overall and by segment (language, geography, risk_band).

metrics.name: authentication_success_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of authentication attempts that successfully complete and allow requested sensitive actions.
metrics.collection_method: Count of calls where authentication_result == 'success' divided by total calls where authentication was attempted.

metrics.name: authentication_failure_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of authentication attempts that fail due to incorrect answers, failed voice verification, failed liveness, or timeouts.
metrics.collection_method: Count of calls where authentication_result in ['failure','timeout'] divided by total calls where authentication was attempted.

metrics.name: call_dropoff_rate_during_auth
metrics.description: Proportion of calls where the caller abandons the call during the authentication stage (before reaching requested service).
metrics.collection_method: Calls with call_disposition == 'abandoned_during_auth' divided by total calls starting authentication.

metrics.name: avg_authentication_time
metrics.description: Average time spent on authentication steps, from the start of the first auth-related prompt/question to the decision to allow/deny access.
metrics.collection_method: Duration measured via system timestamps for auth_start_ts and auth_end_ts.
metrics.aggregation: Mean and percentiles per arm, per risk_band.

metrics.name: avg_total_call_handle_time
metrics.description: Average total call handle time, including IVR and agent talk time, from call answer to call end.
metrics.collection_method: Contact center platform metrics per call_id.

metrics.name: speaker_verification_far
metrics.description: False Acceptance Rate for speaker verification in the treatment arm, estimated from WL2_offline_replay_benchmark and optionally from labeled live incidents.
metrics.collection_method: In offline benchmark, proportion of impostor trials where similarity_score >= threshold; in live, approximate via confirmed fraud calls that passed voice verification.

metrics.name: speaker_verification_frr
metrics.description: False Rejection Rate for speaker verification in the treatment arm.
metrics.collection_method: In offline benchmark, proportion of genuine trials where similarity_score < threshold; in live, approximate via genuine customers (no fraud indicators) who fail verification but pass fallback KBA.
metrics.aggregation: Per language, per demographic segment where available and legally permissible.

metrics.name: liveness_challenge_failure_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of liveness challenges in the treatment arm that fail (ASR mismatch, timing anomaly, or user abandonment).
metrics.collection_method: Count of challenges with liveness_result in ['fail_asr','fail_timing','timeout'] divided by total liveness challenges issued.

metrics.name: csrf_like_replay_detection_rate
metrics.description: Detection rate for replayed or cloned voices in WL2 offline benchmark when passed through the full treatment pipeline.
metrics.collection_method: In WL2, proportion of synthetic or replayed audio sessions correctly rejected by either speaker verification or liveness.

metrics.name: customer_complaint_rate_about_auth
metrics.description: Rate of customer complaints specifically mentioning authentication difficulty, privacy concerns, or confusion about voice verification.
metrics.collection_method: Text-mined or manually labeled complaint tickets and post-call survey responses linked to call_id, filtered by auth-related topics.

metrics.name: biometric_opt_out_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of biometric-enrolled customers who revoke consent or request disabling voice verification during the experiment.
metrics.collection_method: Count of accounts changing biometric_consent_status from true to false divided by total enrolled accounts exposed to treatment.
metrics.aggregation: Per jurisdiction, per arm (treatment specifically, with baseline as control where exposure exists).

metrics.name: system_error_rate
metrics.description: Rate of technical errors in speaker verification or liveness services (e.g., timeouts, 5xx, model exceptions) per call in the treatment arm.
metrics.collection_method: Application logs and metric counters from the verification and liveness services.

primary: The treatment arm achieves at least a 30% relative reduction in fraud_rate_per_10k_calls compared with the baseline arm, with 95% confidence, and no statistically significant increase in fraud_rate_per_10k_calls in any high-risk customer segment.
The avg_total_call_handle_time in the treatment arm does not increase by more than 10% relative to baseline for medium-risk calls, with 95% confidence.
The call_dropoff_rate_during_auth in the treatment arm does not exceed baseline by more than 5 percentage points for any major language or accessibility segment.
secondary: speaker_verification_far in WL2_offline_replay_benchmark is <= 0.5% at an FRR <= 5% for the primary language and channel.
liveness_challenge_failure_rate for genuine callers is <= 10% in the treatment arm, with lower failure rates for customers using accessibility accommodations where measured.

customer_complaint_rate_about_auth in the treatment arm is not more than 20% higher than in the baseline arm and shows no disproportionate increase in protected or vulnerable segments (where measurement is lawful and ethical).
biometric_opt_out_rate remains below a predefined tolerable threshold (e.g., 3% over the experiment window), indicating acceptable customer comfort with the mechanism.
operational: system_error_rate for verification and liveness services remains below 5 errors_per_1000_calls throughout the experiment.
No severe incidents (e.g., major fraud cluster) are attributed to failures unique to the treatment arm; if such incidents occur, the experiment must be paused and design revisited.

failure_modes.name: high_false_rejection_for_specific_segments
failure_modes.description: Speaker verification or liveness has disproportionately high FRR for certain accents, languages, or accessibility needs, leading to discrimination and customer harm.
failure_modes.detection: Monitor speaker_verification_frr and liveness_challenge_failure_rate by segment; investigate if FRR > 2x baseline KBA failure rate for any segment.

failure_modes.name: insufficient_fraud_reduction
failure_modes.description: Despite added friction, the treatment arm does not materially reduce fraud_rate_per_10k_calls compared with baseline.
failure_modes.detection: Interim and final statistical analyses show less than the targeted 30% relative reduction with overlapping confidence intervals or even higher fraud in treatment.

failure_modes.name: increased_social_engineering_via_agents
failure_modes.description: Attackers circumvent voice verification by pressuring or manipulating agents to bypass or override failed verification results.
failure_modes.detection: Audit logs show agents overriding failed voice verification at higher rates in treatment; fraud_events associated with such overrides increase.

failure_modes.name: regulatory_or_privacy_non_compliance
failure_modes.description: Biometric data is processed for callers without valid consent or in prohibited jurisdictions.
failure_modes.detection: Periodic audits show mismatches between consent records and treatment exposure; data protection office flags non-compliance.

failure_modes.name: technical_instability_and_latency_spikes
failure_modes.description: Voice verification or liveness services introduce latency or errors that degrade customer experience beyond acceptable levels.
failure_modes.detection: system_error_rate or avg_authentication_time exceeds predefined SLOs; monitoring alerts or agent feedback highlight systemic slowdowns.

failure_modes.name: adaptive_attacker_evasion
failure_modes.description: Attackers adapt their strategies (e.g., high-quality real-time voice cloning, replay attacks with captured enrollment audio) to bypass verification and liveness, eroding benefits.
failure_modes.detection: Forensically confirmed fraud cases with successful treatment flow outcomes and evidence of synthetic or replayed voices; increased CSRF_like_replay_detection_rate gap between offline and live performance.

failure_modes.name: customer_trust_erosion
failure_modes.description: Customers interpret voice verification as intrusive or risky, leading to higher complaint and opt-out rates.
failure_modes.detection: customer_complaint_rate_about_auth and biometric_opt_out_rate substantially exceed thresholds; surveys show declining satisfaction with authentication.

infrastructure: Telephony/CCaaS platform capable of routing calls through configurable IVR flows and exposing audio streams to external services with low latency.
Application servers (e.g., Python/Node/Java-based) to host the speaker verification and liveness APIs, either in the enterprise environment or a controlled cloud environment.
Feature flag or experimentation platform capable of A/B routing and versioned configuration management.
Risk engine capable of providing risk scores and integrating new signals (speaker_verification_score, liveness_score) via API.
Secure storage for biometric templates (speaker embeddings) with encryption, access control, and auditable access logs.
Observability stack (e.g., Prometheus/Grafana, OpenTelemetry, ELK) for logging metrics, traces, and errors.
software_and_models: Pre-trained speaker verification model(s) from public sources, such as SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN, x-vectors, or similar, along with documentation and licenses compatible with experimental use.
ASR engine for transcribing liveness challenge responses (cloud-based or on-prem).
Liveness scoring component (may initially be rule-based using ASR match and timing signals).
Repository checkout from https://github.com/bookauthority/securing-call containing reference code for embeddings extraction, scoring, and integration stubs (assumes such code will be provided).
data_and_governance: Curated dataset for WL2_offline_replay_benchmark, including labeled genuine and synthetic/replayed audio with associated metadata (language, device, session context).
Enrollment data and consent records for voice biometric-enabled customers.
Data protection impact assessment (DPIA/PIA) and legal sign-off for biometric use in all included jurisdictions.
Policies and procedures for consent, revocation, data retention, and incident response.
teams_and_roles: ML/voice engineering team to integrate and tune speaker verification and liveness components.
Security and fraud team to define risk thresholds, monitor fraud metrics, and investigate incidents.
Contact center operations team to adjust scripts, train agents, and monitor customer feedback.
Privacy/legal team to oversee consent, regulatory compliance, and DPIA/PIA.
Analytics/experiment team to design the A/B test, perform statistical analysis, and interpret results.

run_instructions: Design_and_Approval_Phase

1. Define the specific customer journeys where step-up voice verification and liveness will be introduced (e.g., account recovery, high-value transfers) and ensure alignment with Chapter 7.1 guidance on when to use voice verification.

2. Conduct or update a DPIA/PIA to cover use of voice biometrics and liveness, including cross-jurisdiction analysis, storage, consent, revocation, and purpose limitation in line with Chapter 7.8 and relevant policy chapters.
3. Obtain written approvals from security, fraud, privacy/legal, and contact center leadership for the experimental protocol, including success_criteria, failure_modes, and kill-switch conditions.
4. Define the segments (languages, risk bands, customer categories) to be included and any that must be excluded for regulatory or risk reasons.
Offline_Prototype_and_Threshold_Tuning
5. Implement the speaker verification prototype using public models (Chapter 7.3), following the companion repository’s instructions for feature extraction and scoring.
6. Implement active liveness challenge generation and verification logic as described in Chapter 7.4, ensuring the challenge content is randomized and not trivially predictable or reusable.
7. Assemble WL2_offline_replay_benchmark from historical genuine calls and synthetic/replayed audio; annotate with ground truth labels and metadata.
8. Run WL2 through the speaker verification and liveness components separately and jointly, computing ROC curves, EER, FAR, FRR, and CSRF_like_replay_detection_rate.

9. Choose operating thresholds for speaker_verification_score and liveness_score to achieve target offline FAR/FRR trade-offs as described in the success_criteria. Document these thresholds and configuration versions.

10. Implement risk fusion between the risk engine output, speaker_verification_score, and liveness_score, and validate fusion behavior with synthetic test cases (e.g., low risk + high score, high risk + low score).
Instrumentation_and_Environment_Setup
11. Integrate the prototype speaker verification and liveness services with the telephony/CCaaS platform using reference architectural patterns from Chapter 7.2 and Chapter 8.

12. Implement the A/B routing logic (randomization function, stratification, and assignment to baseline or treatment). Ensure that callers lacking consent are automatically mapped to baseline flow and flagged as 'baseline_only'.
13. Implement detailed logging for each call, including arm assignment, consent status, auth steps performed, scores and thresholds, timings, and outcome fields as described in evidence_schema.
14. Configure monitoring dashboards and alerts for key online metrics: system_error_rate, avg_authentication_time, call_dropoff_rate_during_auth, and any spikes in complaints or fraud indicators.
15. Run end-to-end dry runs in a staging environment with test accounts, validating both baseline and treatment flows, including error handling and fallbacks.
Pilot_and_Ramp_Up

16. Start with a limited pilot (e.g., 5–10% of eligible traffic) in treatment while 90–95% remains in baseline, to validate real-world latency and UX, and to confirm that failure_modes are not triggered.
17. Monitor metrics daily during the pilot, focusing on system_error_rate, call_dropoff_rate_during_auth, customer_complaint_rate_about_auth, and any early fraud indicators.
18. If pilot metrics remain within acceptable ranges for a pre-defined period (e.g., 1–2 weeks), ramp up the treatment allocation to the planned 50/50 split, keeping stratification criteria constant.
Full_Experiment_Run
19. Run the full experiment for at least 4–6 weeks or until sufficient fraud_events accumulate to support the statistical power required for primary success_criteria.

20. During the run, avoid making unplanned model, threshold, or routing changes; if such changes are necessary, document them as configuration version increments and mark the corresponding time windows for separate analysis.

21. Continuously monitor fairness-related metrics (speaker_verification_frr and liveness_challenge_failure_rate by segment) and privacy/compliance controls (e.g., no treatment without consent). Escalate and consider pausing the experiment if severe disparities or compliance issues are detected.
22. Ensure that incident response procedures are followed for any suspected fraud clusters, including cross-checking whether treatment-specific failure_modes contributed.
Post_Experiment_Analysis
23. Compile all call-level and offline benchmark evidence according to the evidence_schema, ensuring de-identification or pseudonymization where required.
24. Compute primary and secondary metrics for each arm and segment; apply appropriate statistical tests (e.g., confidence intervals, hypothesis tests) to determine whether success_criteria are met.

25. Analyze trade-offs across security (fraud_events, fraud_rate_per_10k_calls) and friction (avg_authentication_time, call_dropoff_rate_during_auth, customer_complaint_rate_about_auth) per Chapter 7.5 and Chapter 12 guidance.

26. Investigate fairness and accessibility outcomes (Chapter 7.6): identify any segments where FRR or drop-off is unacceptably high and propose mitigations (e.g., alternative factors, adjusted thresholds, additional agent support).
27. Summarize integration lessons with IAM, risk engines, and fraud systems (Chapter 7.7), including any necessary schema or API changes discovered during the experiment.
28. Document biometric data handling practices, consent flows, and observed opt-out behavior for review with privacy/legal (Chapter 7.8).
Decision_and_Rollout
29. Present findings to cross-functional stakeholders, clearly explaining the observed benefit vs. friction trade-offs and any residual risks or limitations.

30. If success_criteria are met and no unacceptable failure_modes are observed, define a roadmap for expanding treatment to a larger customer population, possibly as the new default authentication step-up path.

31. If results are mixed or negative, identify which components (e.g., liveness design, thresholds, segment targeting) should be iterated and specify the next experimental cycle before any broad rollout.
32. Archive all experiment configurations, code versions, and evidence artifacts for auditability and future reference.

call_level_record.description: One record per inbound call included in the experiment, capturing routing, authentication, scores, outcomes, and key metadata.

call_id.description: Unique identifier for the call within the contact center platform.

account_id.description: Pseudonymized account identifier, hashed or tokenized as per privacy policy.

arm.description: The experimental arm to which this call was assigned.

effective_arm.description: The arm that actually governed the authentication flow, considering fallbacks due to consent, errors, or policy.

risk_band.description: Risk band at call start based on baseline risk engine thresholds.

risk_score_baseline.description: Risk score in [0, 1] from the baseline risk engine at call start.

primary_language.description: Language code (e.g., 'en', 'es') inferred or specified for the call.

device_type.description: Type of calling endpoint where known (e.g., 'mobile', 'landline', 'voip').

biometric_enrollment_status.description: Whether the account was enrolled in voice biometrics at call start.

biometric_consent_status.description: Whether valid biometric consent was recorded and active at call start.

auth_flow_steps.description: Ordered list of authentication steps performed during the call.

speaker_verification_invoked.description: Whether speaker verification was attempted on this call.

speaker_verification_score.description: Normalized speaker verification similarity score in [0, 1], or null if not invoked.

speaker_verification_threshold.description: Decision threshold applied for speaker verification, or null if not invoked.

speaker_verification_result.description: Outcome of speaker verification, if invoked.

liveness_challenge_invoked.description: Whether a liveness challenge was issued during the call.

liveness_score.description: Normalized liveness confidence score in [0, 1], or null if not invoked.

liveness_threshold.description: Decision threshold applied for liveness, or null if not invoked.

liveness_result.description: Outcome of the liveness challenge, if invoked.

combined_auth_risk_score.description: Combined risk score after fusing baseline risk, speaker verification, and liveness where applicable.

auth_result.description: Final outcome of the authentication process.

auth_failure_reason.description: Categorized reason for authentication failure or timeout where applicable (e.g., 'kba_incorrect', 'voice_verification_fail', 'liveness_fail', 'technical_error').

fraud_label.description: Fraud outcome label assigned after investigations and post-call data become available.

fraud_label_source.description: Source of fraud labeling (e.g., 'chargeback', 'fraud_team_review', 'customer_report'), or null if not labeled.

fraud_label_ts.description: Timestamp when fraud label was assigned, if any (ISO 8601).

customer_feedback_code.description: Code or label summarizing any auth-related customer feedback (e.g., from post-call survey).

auth_complaint_flag.description: True if customer raised a complaint about authentication during or after the call.

biometric_opt_out_flag.description: True if the customer opted out of biometric authentication during or immediately after the call.

system_error_flags.description: List of technical error codes encountered during speaker verification or liveness processing.

config_version.description: Version identifier for the configuration (models, thresholds, routing rules) active for this call.

offline_trial_record.description: One record per trial in the WL2_offline_replay_benchmark dataset, capturing verification and liveness outcomes under controlled conditions.

trial_id.description: Unique identifier for the offline trial.

dataset_id.description: Identifier for the dataset or corpus from which this trial is drawn.

trial_type.description: Ground truth class of the trial.

cloning_tool_id.description: Identifier for the cloning or replay tool used for synthetic/replay trials, if applicable.

speaker_id.description: Pseudonymized identifier for the true speaker.

enrolled_speaker_id.description: Speaker ID of the target enrollment profile in impostor/synthetic/replay trials.

audio_duration_sec.description: Duration of the audio sample used for verification.

speaker_verification_score.description: Similarity score from the speaker verification model.

speaker_verification_threshold.description: Threshold applied for pass/fail decision in this evaluation run.

speaker_verification_result.description: Result of speaker verification for this trial.

liveness_challenge_type.description: Type of synthetic liveness challenge used, if any.

liveness_threshold.description: Threshold applied for liveness decision in this evaluation run.

liveness_result.description: Liveness outcome for this trial, if applicable.

combined_auth_risk_score.description: Combined score from simulated fusion logic, if applied.
